title: Zanclean flood
summary: About 5.33 million years ago the Mediterranean, which had been cut off from the ocean and largely dried out, was refilled by Atlantic water through the Strait of Gibraltar. A channel about 200 km long crosses the strait. Modelling suggests early discharge near 100 million cubic metres per second, with about 90% of the water transferred in a few months to two years.

uncertainty.note: The pages give 5.33 (Nature 2009) and 5.3 (Earth-Science Reviews 2020) Ma without an error bar. Garcia-Castellanos et al. say flooding began with low discharges that may have lasted up to several thousand years before the main phase.

as_recorded.value: end of the Messinian Salinity Crisis at 5.3 million years ago

where.historical_name: Strait of Gibraltar between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean basin; Late Miocene to Early Pliocene, no polities

importance.justification: A proposed megaflood that refilled an entire sea, with discharge far above any river today.

related.because: The flood refilled the Mediterranean basin after the Messinian salinity crisis had cut it off from the ocean.
